text:
incbot: :rotating_light: ALERT — inference-gateway-private: spike in 5xx (504/502) and timeouts from private VPC peering (us-west-2) to model-hosting cluster. breach of latency SLOs. auto-escalation to on-call. root_ts=3411110000
anya_oncall: seeing it. joining. paging @taylor_neteng and @mike_sre.
anya_oncall: quick QA: is customer-facing API returning 504s or are background jobs?
alice_support: customers reporting API timeouts for embeddings and streaming endpoints — support tickets from tenant-321, tenant-88, tenant-internal-prod.
taylor_neteng: I have console open. BGP peering looks stable; control plane fine. CP metrics show increased retransmits to our peering appliance. NAT gateway metrics: ephemeral_port_utilization high, conntrack_count near limit.
mike_sre: logs from inference-gateway show repeated upstream connect timeouts to backend pool (model-hosting-private). snippet: ```
[2026-03-15T12:03:21Z] gateway: upstream request failed: dial tcp 10.20.5.12:443: i/o timeout -> 504
[2026-03-15T12:03:23Z] gateway: upstream request failed: connection reset by peer -> 502
```
anya_oncall: ok likely NAT/translation issue. do we have a quick mitigation to restore traffic?
taylor_neteng: a few options: 1) failover route to standby NAT gateway in same AZ (fast) 2) widen ephemeral port range + bump conntrack_max (safer but takes few mins to propagate) 3) temporary LB-level proxy to route through public egress for affected subnets.
anya_oncall: try 1) and 2) in parallel. mike, can you coordinate the gateway config changes?
mike_sre: doing failover to standby NAT now. running: ```bash
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0abc123 --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --nat-gateway-id nat-0standby
```
mike_sre: route replace returned OK, waiting <30s for drift to clear. metrics: outbound pkts via nat-0primary dropped from 8k/s -> 2k/s, nat-0standby rising to 6k/s.
taylor_neteng: pushing conntrack bump: ```bash
# on peering transit appliance (root)
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range="15000 65535"
```
taylor_neteng: conntrack count before: 65529, after sysctl: 65529 still until new connections open; should free as sessions close. also increased ephemeral range to reduce collisions.
alice_support: support note: "We are seeing a subset of API traffic returning 504s from private VPC customers in us-west-2. Engineering is actively mitigating. ETA for full mitigation unknown, partial routing restored."
sam_product: any risk to stateful model sessions / KV cache?
mike_sre: sessions that rely on persistent connections to model-hosting (long-lived websockets) will experience resets; short requests should recover quicker after failover.
deploy-bot: Deploy succeeded: rollback of recent transit appliance config (id: roll-2026-03-15-12:01) completed.
taylor_neteng: note — I see a pattern: NAT gateway SNAT ports per connection cluster exceeded for client IP blocks from peering. likely port exhaustion due to sudden burst of client IPs after canary traffic shift earlier. adding standby NAT reduced immediate failure rate.
anya_oncall: good. can we rate-limit or add aggressive keepalive timeouts on gateway to avoid lingering sockets?
mike_sre: lowered keepalive_ttl on gateway proxy and enabled quicker connection reuse: changed proxy config -> ```yaml
upstream:
  keepalive_timeout: 15s
  reuse_connections: true
```
mike_sre: applying now.
alice_support: customer impact update: approx 9-14% 5xx rate at peak for private-VPC customers in us-west-2 between 12:00–12:20 UTC (rolling window). highest impact tenant-321 (analytics jobs) showing 30% failure on batch runs.
taylor_neteng: running conntrack cleanup on transit appliance to relieve stale entries: ```bash
# list heavy conntrack entries
echo "show conntrack" | conntrack -L | grep ESTABLISHED | wc -l
# flush orphaned
conntrack -D -s 10.20.0.0/16
```
taylor_neteng: flushed many entries for the affected subnet, conntrack_count dropped to 18k.
mike_sre: after route failover + conntrack bump + proxy keepalive changes, 5xx rate dropped to ~2.3% in last 5m. monitoring for recurrence.
anya_oncall: temp mitigation worked. what's next for durable fix?
taylor_neteng: ACTIONS: 1) schedule NAT autoscaling (add NATs to pool + automated failover) 2) increase default conntrack_max and ephemeral range for transit appliances 3) implement egress path diversity in peering runbook 4) add alert on ephemeral_port_utilization > 80% and conntrack nearing limit 5) investigate origin of burst (was there a traffic shaping change?)
sam_product: add a follow-up to optimize client-side connection pooling in SDKs to reduce ephemeral port use.
alice_support: I've sent templated customer outbound to affected tenants with mitigation summary and ETA for permanent fixes.
deploy-bot: Postmortem draft created: https://redwood.internal/incident/3411110000 (editable).
anya_oncall: handing off to @mike_sre for evening oncall. summary for handoff: incident started 3411110000 UTC, root cause: NAT ephemeral/conntrack exhaustion triggered by sudden client-IP burst across peering -> upstream timeouts. mitigations applied: route failover to standby NAT, conntrack_max bump, ephemeral range expansion, proxy keepalive tuning, conntrack cleanup. current status: stable, 5xx ~2% and trending to <1%. customer impact: peaked ~12% overall private-vpc 5xx, tenant-321 worst. actions remaining: automated NAT autoscaling + runbook updates + alert tuning + postmortem.
mike_sre: acknowledged, will monitor and own follow-ups. leaving a runbook checklist in the incident doc.
anya_oncall: thanks team. closing live channel but will keep incident doc open for postmortem edits. :checkered_flag:
